I can’t read the GitHub Actions logs for PR `#888` directly here because `gh auth status` shows the local GitHub CLI token is invalid, but I was able to reproduce a real failure on the PR branch locally.

The meaningful failure is `TestCopilotVSCodeHooks_GeneratedHookCommands` in [copilot_vscode_hooks_test.go](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/vscode-hooks/cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/copilot_vscode_hooks_test.go:126). Running

```bash
env GOCACHE=/tmp/go-build go test -tags=integration ./cmd/entire/cli/integration_test -run 'TestCopilotVSCodeHooks_GeneratedHookCommands' -count=1
```

fails with:

```text
failed to parse hook event: failed to parse hook input: json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field userPromptSubmittedRaw.timestamp of type int64
```

The likely root cause is the test helper, not the new Copilot parser itself. The direct Copilot hook path passes, and the focused Copilot package tests pass. But `resolveHookCommand()` only rewrites commands that start with `entire ` directly in [copilot_vscode_hooks_test.go](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/vscode-hooks/cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/copilot_vscode_hooks_test.go:273). The generated hook commands in production mode are wrapped with `sh -c '... exec entire hooks copilot-cli ...'` by [hook_command.go](/Users/peytonmontei/Documents/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/vscode-hooks/cmd/entire/cli/agent/hook_command.go:30), so the helper never rewrites them to the freshly built test binary. That means the integration test ends up executing whatever `entire` is on `PATH`, which appears to be an older binary that still expects `timestamp` as an `int64`.

So the short version is: the PR’s new parser is working in the in-process and direct hook paths, but the generated-hook integration test is still invoking the wrong binary. If you want, I can patch that helper so wrapped production commands also resolve to `getTestBinary()` and then rerun the relevant tests.
